title: A Mech Is Continued
summary: Tessell can rebuild almost every part of a walker except the root that makes it one.
body: Every walker begins with a root frame: the reactor cradle, central keel, control lattice and gait interfaces buried in its centre torso. The root fixes the machine's mass, stride and structural mounts. A shop can work around those facts. It cannot make new ones.

Open an old Compact hull, cut away what seized, re-armour it in Sarn plate and hang whatever the local works can keep fed. The result may share no visible part with the machine in the depot ledger. Under the welds, the same serialized root is still carrying the load.

The Authority calls a walker by that serial. Crews give it a name. Shops add a mark for each passage through the gantry. Root, name and shop mark are three records of one physical machine, not three machines that can be ordered from a catalogue.

This is why two walkers of the same class are never identical, why a company that loses one cannot simply build another, and why the most valuable thing on a battlefield is the wreck still standing at dusk.

Take the legs and you have a named machine that may walk again. Break the centre torso and the walker falls; if its cradle survives the breach, recovery begins there. If it does not, the root, the name and every claim on its next life end together.
